event.summary: Verify decoder removal cannot strand supported old terminals
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Removing the decoder would make still-supported old terminals unusable and could lose running work if removal implicitly terminates them. Source basis: assigned deletion removes pane discovery, control framing, replay cutover, passthrough decoding and their tests. SPEC_impl.md at this revision, Terminal substrate: private tmux server, explicitly says: "The running supervisor runs no tmux at all, and its driver of the old terminals is gone: what remains is the startup step that ends them" and "A failure anywhere is logged and never fatal (the maintainer chose to start anyway and treat old sessions as ended, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running)". Suggested bucket: potentially highest (running user processes); confidence: source-backed lead requiring caller/startup checks. proposed_drop: not decided; intentional retirement is an apparent specification basis, but validate actual startup ordering and replacement callers before settlement. possible_cover: specification acceptance quoted above; no other coverage sources read. Checks so far: entire assigned patch packet lines 1-1289 read, pinned retirement section read fully. Missing premise: whether startup actually gates reload and old terminal rows avoid the removed APIs. Next check: pinned lib/core startup and terminal-host dispatch. No execution or reproduction performed.

event.summary: Old terminal work and history intentionally end before decoder removal
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: An upgrade ends programs still running in old terminals and discards their screen/scrollback; if cleanup fails, those programs can remain inaccessible and Restart may start another beside them. This potentially highest consequence (user-owned processes/work) is retained for independent proposed-drop review because the specification explicitly accepts it. Source: deletion removes the old decoder and pane discovery (original control_codec.rs:1-849, assigned patch lines 1-855). At the reviewed revision service/core.rs:6112-6117 checks the store first; 6142-6151 gates end_private_server on state-directory ownership before 6168-6184 reloads sessions. core/old_terminals.rs:176-233 identifies the socket peer and invokes verified termination without a tmux binary. core.rs:6675-6679 always resolves old-kind rows as no terminal, 6805-6822 converts live old rows to TerminalEnded, and 7042-7090 sweeps before committing conversions and recording notices. service/terminals.rs:122-127,225-248 resolves only host runtimes, with old-agent absence explained at 195-207. Pinned git grep across crates found no remaining references to control_codec, read_command_block, PassthroughDecoder, parse_pane_facts or unescape_control_output. Suggested bucket: highest if treated as a bug. Could-be-highest: yes, established process-ending route. Confidence: confirmed by source and specification, not execution. proposed_drop: explicit specification acceptance. Exact SPEC.md Terminal experience text at this revision, lines 3003-3016: 'This release ends them: the first time a host’s supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program.' [The source uses an ASCII apostrophe in host's.] Also: 'one whose agent had already ended keeps its outcome, but its terminal’s last screen, which lived in the server, is gone; old tabs are closed.' [The source uses an ASCII apostrophe in terminal's.] Also: 'A failure to end the server or to stop what ran there is logged and never stops the supervisor from starting; those sessions are treated as ended all the same, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running.' SPEC_impl.md Terminal substrate: private tmux server, lines 2882-2889: 'This release ends them at startup (below); every terminal runs in a terminal host' and 'The running supervisor runs no tmux at all, and its driver of the old terminals is gone'. These rules accept the full original consequence; removal does not independently introduce a still-supported terminal path requiring this decoder. possible_cover: quoted specifications only; no queue/coverage search performed. Caveat: caller must independently judge the proposed drop because of its highest consequence. No tests or reproductions performed; this concerns retirement/removal implications, not unrelated defects in retired parser code.

event.summary: Removing the tmux line cap does not remove the active transport's bounds
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR considered: deleting read_control_line and MAX_CONTROL_LINE might allow terminal output to consume unbounded supervisor memory or accept truncated replay. Suggested bucket if established: high (terminal/control availability); could-be-highest: no established security or work-loss route; terminal hosts retain running programs independently. Confidence: confirmed source refutation for this removal. proposed_drop: source refutation, not specification-only acceptance. The deleted bounds applied only to the retired tmux newline protocol. Active host transport hosts/client.rs:1016-1049 decodes buffered messages before each further read and enforces deadlines, 1078-1099 passes MAX_FRAME into split_frame and rejects malformed frames; terminal-host/src/protocol.rs:322-340 rejects zero/oversized declared lengths as soon as four bytes arrive and waits for the whole declared frame, while 777-783 caps each Output at MAX_OUTPUT_CHUNK and rejects empty output. The assigned deletion has no surviving callers (pinned git grep of crates for control_codec/read_command_block/PassthroughDecoder/parse_pane_facts/unescape_control_output returned no matches). SPEC_impl.md Terminal host, lines 1963-1980, declares each terminal's separate host protocol and old-terminal retirement; the frame checks are on that replacement path, not dependent on the removed line parser. possible_cover: none searched. Caveats: not a full independent audit of the host transport's resource accounting; conclusion is limited to deletion of this codec. No execution/reproduction performed.

event.summary: Retiring tmux notification decoding does not remove host replay or pane isolation
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR considered: removal of command-block cutover validation, pane-id filtering and passthrough provenance might mix neighboring terminals or manufacture/repeat replay output. Confidence: confirmed source refutation for the codec deletion. Suggested bucket if established: high for corrupted terminal display; could-be-highest: no established route from this removal to security impact or loss of work. proposed_drop: source refutation. Each active terminal resolves to a HostTerminal (service/terminals.rs:225-248,259-265); hosts/terminal.rs:1-43 describes its own connection, raw-output journal and replay boundaries rather than a session-wide tmux control stream. Active output messages carry bytes and a journal offset, terminal-host/src/protocol.rs:777-783; there is no tmux notification grammar or octal transform to decode. hosts/terminal.rs:3424-3435 skips bytes below the processed offset, 3449-3503 splits feeds at seen/unseen/live journal boundaries, and 2728-2773 chooses the corresponding FeedMode. The same-commit diff of hosts/terminal.rs leaves these replay functions unchanged. SPEC_impl.md Terminal host, Recovery and checkpoints, lines 2130-2143 explicitly defines those byte-bound replay effects; the active stream therefore does not depend on the deleted command-block or pane-id machinery. The deleted tests pin a transport that no active terminal uses, and their removal does not alone establish a test gap for this group's assigned change. possible_cover: none searched. Caveats: this is a deletion-contract check, not an independent audit of the replacement emulator or host protocol. No execution or reproductions performed.

event.summary: Retained tests distinguish active replay effects and terminal isolation
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. Original TLDR considered: 'removal of command-block cutover validation, pane-id filtering and passthrough provenance might mix neighboring terminals or manufacture/repeat replay output.' Suggested bucket if established: high for corrupted terminal display; could-be-highest: no established security/work-loss route from this deletion. Confidence: source-refuted for this removal, not executed. proposed_drop: source refutation; independent checker remains free to reject it. Original production basis remains service/terminals.rs:225-248,259-265 (specific host runtime), terminal-host/src/protocol.rs:777-783 (raw bytes plus offset), hosts/terminal.rs:3424-3503,2728-2773 (duplicate skipping and seen/unseen/live boundaries), unchanged replay functions in the same-commit diff. Synthesis explicitly checked test sensitivity instead of inferring it from correct production. Retained hosts/terminal/tests.rs:336-350 puts seen/unseen/live bytes in one Output and asserts exactly STATUS_ANSWER then DA1_ANSWER plus caught_up; 405-414 puts seen query in a synchronized update closed by live bytes and asserts only the live status answer; 536-586 distinguishes snapshot, seen, unseen and live queries/OSC52 and asserts only the unseen status answer and live clipboard notice, with a final status roundtrip before asserting no more notices. Retained farhelm/tests/e2e/terminal_tabs.rs:1339-1393 attaches agent and tab on one client connection, sends distinct markers to each, verifies positive delivery, drains both and asserts neither transcript contains the other's marker. By source inspection these observables distinguish duplicate/wrong-zone effects and mixed-terminal output; they exercise active host responsibilities rather than the retired control-mode grammar. Deleted command-block/notification/passthrough tests called retired APIs and are not the only assertions protecting those surviving responsibilities. Governing contract: SPEC_impl.md Terminal host, Recovery and checkpoints, lines 2130-2143 defines seen/unseen/live effects and one-runtime terminal isolation. possible_cover: none searched. Caveats: no assertion of exhaustive coverage or mutation-test execution; this only refutes a defect attributed to removing this codec's tests. All original consequences preserved above.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR considered: removing authoritative pane-fact/marker joins could let tab Close act on an agent or another tab, terminating work the user did not authorize. Suggested bucket if established: highest; could-be-highest: yes, wrong-target process termination. Confidence: source-refuted for the assigned decoder removal; no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation, pending caller independent check, not an accepted drop. Removed parse_pane_facts_flagged/join_pane_markers operate solely on the retired tmux driver's mutable window-option text. Replacement host identity uses the host's tag and the session's own HostTab cell: core/host_tabs.rs:1279-1405 builds records per session/tab, passes only named sockets to discovery and checks names_tab before adoption; 1474-1479 requires exact session id AND Tab role AND tab id. close_host_tab_under_claim at 915-929 rechecks both tab id and the runtime handle and refuses the agent runtime; 932-943 refuses an unreadable host; 964-969 rechecks automatic reap eligibility. Failed termination at 1026-1037 retains the tab for retry, while 1013-1024 forgets it only after end_tab_host succeeded. end_tab_host at 1052-1062 checks the adopted process even when the runtime says Gone. Thus the new path neither parses tmux option rows nor loses an identity check supplied by this codec. Contract: pinned SPEC_impl.md Tabs in hosts, 2331-2343, requires the tag/cell/agent-runtime checks and preservation on unconfirmed end. Exact source supplies the refutation; specification acceptance of deliberate old-terminal retirement is not being extended to this separate unauthorized-termination consequence. possible_cover: none searched. Caveats: limited to consequences of deleting this codec and its discovery helper; this is not a full independent audit of every host lifecycle implementation. Original wrong-target/security/loss-of-work consequence is preserved for later independent checking.
